reporter.title: MemLLM: Finetuning LLMs to Use Explicit Read-Write Memory

rows.variant: Mistral-7B-v0.1 (original, no finetuning)
rows.notes: Perplexity (lower is better), not a 0-100 score. OVERALL = all tokens, TARGET = target entities (entities a memory read could supply), ENTITY = all named entities (§4.2). p(w_i) mixes the with-read and without-read continuation by the probability of emitting '({' (§4.2); reads are only scored at the evaluation data's read positions (footnote 3), so the authors say these PPLs are upper bounds for MemLLM. Eval text: the paper says 'Re-DocRED test' and the Table 2 caption calls it Re-DocRED's validation set. Baseline #1 in Table 2: the base model the authors finetune; run by the authors.

ZsRE, 1000 sequential edits, Mistral-7B. Scores x100 from the paper's 0-1 values. Overall = AVG of REL, GEN, LOC (Table 3). Locality prompts from NQ (§4.3). Edits are appended to the question as 'It is or they are X' inside ({USER_ST})...({USER_END}), written to memory by the write model, and read back with a 5-shot QA prompt whose last shot shows a memory read (§4.3). Released eval script scores reliability as 'edit string contained in the generated answer' (eval_zsre.py L246), a different measure from the copied baselines; it also evaluates each edit right after writing it, with only earlier edits in memory (L237-L250), and gather_zsre_result.py drops prompts containing 'sex' or 'gender'. Thresholds per App. D: tau_e 0.85, tau_t 0.2, tau_r 0.6 (code: REL_SIM 0.5).
